findings.obligation: P4 and the decision that the control carries aria-controls pointing at the rail primary navigation: every required production effect must be declared in the design the crafter is given.
findings.observation: The oracle resolves aria-controls through document.getElementById and requires it to be the rail nav element (controlsTheNav), which is the faithful reading of the decision. No shipped markup supplies that id: templates/partials/sidebar.html renders <nav class="sidebar__nav" aria-label="Primary"> with no id, and no aria-controls exists anywhere in templates or static/js today. The design declares sidebar.html UnchangedCompatible and outside the editable set, and it lists only two effects for the new asset, the document attribute write and the storage write, so the artifact that supplies the id is undeclared. Non-blocking: the asset that builds the button can set the id when absent, so the chain is constructible and craft is not blocked.
findings.remediation: Amend the design one line: state that the collapse asset assigns an id to the rail primary navigation when it is absent, as a third declared DOM effect of that asset, or declare partials/sidebar.html as Extend for exactly one id attribute. Do not widen the editable set further.

findings.obligation: P4: the toggle states in its accessible name OR its state whether the nav is expanded or collapsed. Expectation E9 reads the same way. An oracle must permit every equivalent valid observation of the selected criterion.
findings.observation: The oracle requires the accessible name to contain the lowercase substring nav, in addition to reading the state exactly from aria-expanded and requiring the name to change with the press. Neither the promise nor the design decision fixes that vocabulary; the decision only says the aria-label names the current state and what the next press does, in the shape theme.js describe() already uses, and the shipped theme label is "Theme: following your device. Switch to light.", which names its subject without the word nav. An equally valid implementation labelling the same control "Sidebar: expanded. Hide the sidebar." satisfies P4 and is refused here, which would read as a false RED during craft. The rest of the name assertion, non-empty and changed by the press, is well grounded and should stay.
findings.remediation: Accept the authority vocabulary rather than one token: require the name to contain any of nav, navigation, sidebar or menu, or have the design state the naming constraint explicitly; keep the non-empty and changed-by-the-press arms unchanged.

The RED is semantic, not BROKEN. All 31 failures are step panics naming absent production behaviour: 26 on the absent control (press_the_control and assert_control_reports, webdriver "no such element" for .sidebar__brand button[aria-expanded]), 1 on the absent document mark on a railless screen, 1 on the fold asset never being fetched (anti-vacuity guard of the storage-refused row), the rest on the same control through the phone and stored-choice rows. The single pass, "With scripting off the left nav is open and there is no control at all", is the already-satisfied P5 promise and must stay green; its vacuity guards (rail present, keyboard-layer marker absent, both nav items usable) are in the same scenario.

Obligation-to-observation closure is total in both directions. Forward: P1 geometry (released width equals gained width within 1.5px, rail plus content equal shell, stored sentinel), P2 persistence (reload and other page, three pages with the stored byte unchanged, served render-blocking tag plus paint timing), P3 reopen (shipped 240px, items laid out, visible and focusable, key absent, still open after reload, two-press identity from both start states), P4 keyboard (Tab walk to the control, real Enter and real Space, focus kept with a 2px outline, button element, exact aria-expanded, aria-controls resolving to the rail nav, non-empty name that changes with the press), P5 degraded (scripting-off session, document sweep for any keyboard-reachable nav control, railless screen, storage-refused screen), P6 phone (320, 390 and 480 logical px, each with and without the stored sentinel, document scrollWidth against viewport, column shell, bar-width rail, board strip scrolling inside itself). Laws L1-L7 each have at least one falsifier; L8 is the architectural gate obligation T1 in xtask, outside this oracle and not duplicated by it. Reverse: every assertion in the module traces to a promise, a law, an admitted state (two-tab divergence, foreign stored value, valued mark) or a declared stressor (Y9 focus order, Y10 phone, Y11 longest name); none observes an undeclared fact.

Constructibility checked against the shipped substrate, every support fact present before craft. browser_harness.rs declares new_session (408), new_dark_session_refusing_site_storage (452), unhandled_script_errors (502), new_session_without_scripting (687), sign_in_through_browser (879), press_key (976) and BOARD_READY_SELECTOR (1126); key_chord maps Enter, Space and Tab to the WebDriver private-use code points, so the Space row presses a key and does not type a word. FoundryWorld declares harness, http and browser; the reused Background from feature_board_new_issue.rs populates harness and http, so served_dashboard_html can run. signed_in_get(harness, http, email, password, url) returns PostOutcome with status and body. The anti-vacuity arm of the no-flash step holds on the shipped shell: templates/base.html declares eight head scripts, one render-blocking (theme.js, line 47) and seven carrying defer, so head.len() >= 2 and deferred_neighbours > 0 are satisfied rather than unsatisfiable. The 2px focus assertion is met by the shipped .sidebar :focus-visible rule (outline 2px solid). The probe selectors exist in partials/sidebar.html and the stylesheet: .sidebar (flex 0 0 240px), .sidebar__brand, .sidebar__monogram, .sidebar__workspace, .sidebar__nav with exactly two .sidebar__item anchors, .sidebar__user, and the shipped 480px block already sets width auto and flex 0 0 auto. The one new support capability, open_mobile_session_sized, keeps open_mobile_session as a 390x844 wrapper, so no shipped caller changes. Direct store writes in the long-name Given follow the shipped step convention (718 sqlx::query uses across the step modules).

Lane and budget facts. The feature file tags every scenario @needs-browser @real-io; tests/acceptance.rs excludes needs-browser from the default lane (line 351) and includes it in the all lane, so these 32 cases add no default-suite time and no infrastructure-suite derogation is needed. Positive single-tag selection (acceptance.rs 261-299) honours any scenario tag, which is how FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=nav-collapse-toggle and the per-group tags select. The hazard the design records as Y8 is real and not an oracle defect: a gate run without FOUNDRY_XTASK_INCLUDE_DOCKER=1 observes none of these scenarios, so completion evidence must name the lane that actually ran. Default budgets apply unchanged, no timing measurement is in scope at this phase, and no half-budget or derogation claim was made that would require nine sequential runs. Port treatment is real at every declared port: a real browser against the same in-process origin, the real origin localStorage key, the real document attribute channel and the real served markup. No fake and no @in-memory marker appears anywhere in the oracle, so no fake stands where a declared failure must be observed.

Declared limits judged, and two minor imprecisions judged non-blocking. The two NotTested dispositions are authority-backed, not hidden gaps: the pixels of the first painted frame are an Unknown owned by the solution architect (E4 itself states frame-level capture is required), and the oracle still observes the two available layers, the served render-blocking tag shape (deterministic, load-bearing) and first-contentful-paint timing (supporting); a press with site storage refused on a signed-in page is unreachable by construction because refusing site storage also blocks the session cookie, which is the exclusion the theme feature already recorded. The broad half of L5, arbitrary strings an outside writer can leave, has no generated property: the pure core is JavaScript and the repository has no JS runner, which the design records as an explicit DEVIATION with the host as risk owner; the six example rows plus the valueless-mark construction claim are its projection, and reopening that settled decision is outside this review. Imprecision, non-blocking: the no-flash scenario navigates to the project board in the live browser but parses the served markup of the dashboard; both extend the one shell template base.html and the whole set of pre-paint tags is governed by the T1 gate obligation, so no plausible wrong behaviour escapes.

Business-language and observable-behaviour check. Scenario titles and step phrases are the operator view throughout (folds the left nav away, comes back, opens it again, says which way the left nav is set, with scripting off there is no control at all); no title or step carries a production symbol, a file name, the storage key, the attribute name, a slice id or an ADR number, and the step texts are unique within the feature. The one place technical vocabulary appears in a step, "from a script the browser may not defer past the first paint", is the declared observation channel for a promise whose pixels are not observable, so it is a promised mechanism rather than incidental plumbing. Every assertion reads a return value or a public observation: rendered widths, computed display, document attribute presence, accessible name and aria-expanded, keyboard focus and its outline, scrollWidth against viewport, element counts, the stored value at the declared origin key, and the browser own unhandled-error record. No private field, no mock, no call count, no prose pin. Each "nothing went wrong" observation carries its own anti-vacuity arm: the mechanism must agree with the origin before any overflow or bar-geometry measurement, the error recorder is proved with a deliberate uncaught throw, the asset must have been fetched on the storage-refused load, the Tab walk must have made at least two stops, and the served-markup parse must see deferring attributes on the neighbours it is not asserting about.

Independence of the oracle expectations. No expected value is taken from production under test, which does not exist yet: the open rail width 240px is the shipped stylesheet value the authority constrains to stay (.sidebar flex 0 0 240px), the storage key foundry.nav and the single sentinel collapsed come from the ADR and its agreement rows, the breakpoint 480px comes from the product bound and the shipped media query, the 24-character workspace name is the ceiling the database rule enforces, and the released-width equality is derived from P1 rather than from any rule. The folded strip width is deliberately never named, so the design value can move without touching the oracle; every folded assertion is relative, either narrower than the open rail in the same session or equal to the width the valueless mark produces in the same document.

diagnostic: ACCEPTED for craft. The public oracle is constructible, independent and complete against the agreed value, and its RED is semantic. Criteria adequacy first: P1-P6 preserve the original request (a collapsible left nav that stays collapsed until the operator expands it) and add no narrowing; the only exclusion, syncing across browsers, devices and accounts, is human-authorized and was never promised. Closure is total in both directions over P1-P6 and L1-L7, with L8 carried by the T1 architectural-gate obligation outside this oracle and not duplicated by it; the two NotTested dispositions are authority-backed (first-frame pixels are an architect-owned Unknown with the render-blocking tag shape and paint timing observed instead; a press with site storage refused on a signed-in page is unreachable because that setting also blocks the session cookie). Every scenario drives the declared public boundary in a real browser against the real origin, with real assets, real keystrokes, real mobile emulation at 320, 390 and 480 px and the real stored key; no fake, no @in-memory marker, no private import, no mock assertion, no prose pin. Each quiet-outcome observation carries its own anti-vacuity arm, including a proved error recorder, a fetched-asset guard, a mechanism-agrees-with-the-origin guard and a deferring-neighbour guard. RED evidence: the reused 32-case run (31 failed on absent control, mark or asset; 1 already-satisfied P5 green; 0 parsing and 0 hook errors) plus a new execution of the degraded lane at 53ffb7f that reproduces 2 semantic RED and the 1 green with identical panic text. Two findings, both non-blocking and neither invalidating this phase: design owes one line naming the artifact that supplies the aria-controls target id, since the rail navigation has none and the template is declared unchanged; oracle should widen the accessible-name subject requirement from the single token nav to the authority vocabulary, which would otherwise refuse an equivalent valid label. Capability limit: typesafe unavailable (exit 3, key absent), so every judgment here is reviewer_reason from local evidence. Completion obligations retained: implementation GREEN for all 32 cases, and close evidence that names the lane that actually ran, because a gate without Docker observes none of these scenarios.
